item.title: Casino gambling on back-burner
item.description: The odds of lawmakers approving casino gambling in 2026 basically went to zero this week when the S.C. House voted to return a bill that would OK a proposed Santee-area casino to the Ways and Means Committee. The post Casino gambling on back-burner appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: S.C. House passes bathroom bill
item.description: After a sometimes contentious two-day debate, members of the S.C. House voted 96-19 on Jan. 29 to require people in state schools and colleges to use bathrooms and changing facilities that match their birth sex. The post S.C. House passes bathroom bill appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Kronsberg to be new leader of Charleston Parks Conservancy
item.description: Charleston native and veteran parks leader Jason Kronsberg has been named the new executive director of the Charleston Parks Conservancy. Its board announced his appointment Thursday. The post Kronsberg to be new leader of Charleston Parks Conservancy appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Photo essay: More cold ahead on snow day
item.description: Weather officials on a sunny Sunday morning warned Charleston-area residents to be safe if traveling as Saturday night snow will make roads icy and potentially dangerous. The post Photo essay: More cold ahead on snow day appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Bitter cold persists; Rain on the way at mid-week
item.description: MORNING HEADLINES | The Lowcountry didn’t get as much snow as some expected, but the bitter temperatures numbed fingers and noses across the weekend – and that will continue today. The post Bitter cold persists; Rain on the way at mid-week appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: At least 6 die in S.C. in winter storm
item.description: The frigid impacts of the weekend storm named Ferm are now being linked to six deaths in South Carolina, officials say. The post At least 6 die in S.C. in winter storm appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Stopping West Ashley sewer overflow is focus of new agreement
item.description: A new agreement between two Charleston water groups seeks to address a smelly problem: overflowing sewage in problem areas of West Ashley. The post Stopping West Ashley sewer overflow is focus of new agreement appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: McCorkle: Ten Commandments bill won’t actually do much
item.description: A bill at the Statehouse (H. 4762) that would require the Ten Commandments in every South Carolina classroom jumped its first hurdle on Jan. 21 when a House Judiciary subcommittee favorably approved it to the full committee for consideration. The post McCorkle: Ten Commandments bill won’t actually do much appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Settlement offers living conditions reforms at juvenile center
item.description: A five-year civil lawsuit over the living conditions at the Charleston County Juvenile Detention Center (CCJDC) has ended with a settlement that outlines reforms for the facility. The post Settlement offers living conditions reforms at juvenile center appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Review: Passion, pragmatism square off in Austen’s sister act
item.description: Resplendent silk and burnished wood. Frothy quips and impossible curls. Plus, there’s all of that push-me, pull-you of sense and sensibility that dogs the dowry-meager Dashwood sisters as they find out what love has to do with it all.
